title: FL hosts event for children empowerment
summary: First Lady Liza Marcos yesterday hosted an event for “Fostering the Future Together,” a global coalition launched by US First Lady Melania Trump to empower children through technology and…

blocks.text: First Lady Liza Marcos joins the spouses of world leaders attending the 49th Asean Summit at the ‘Fostering the Future Together’ conference at the Hilton Manila in Pasay on November 16, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — First Lady Liza Marcos yesterday hosted an event for “Fostering the Future Together,” a global coalition launched by US First Lady Melania Trump to empower children through technology and education.
The US first lady did not attend the event at the Hilton Manila in Pasay City but delivered a video message.
In her message, Trump said nearly 60 nations have joined the coalition and “are actively advancing this mission.”
US Ambassador Lee Lipton, in his remarks, said the US first lady believes that children deserve every opportunity to succeed.
Melania met Liza in New York in September, according to Lipton.
Marcos said “while technology opens so many wonderful doors, it also brings dangers to many of us.”
She said cyberbullying, online exploitation, harmful content and people who take advantage of children’s innocence are very real concerns.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in the country today to attend the ASEAN-US Special Summit.
Trump is also set to hold a bilateral meeting with President Marcos during his visit, ASEAN 2026 spokesman Dominic Xavier Imperial confirmed earlier.
US has been an ASEAN dialogue partner since 1977.

A Pax Silica deal is unlikely to be finalized during Trump’s visit, as the Philippines and the US are still working on details of such an agreement, Philippine Ambassador to Washington Jose Manuel Romualdez earlier said.
Lipton also said there are no plans for the signing of agreements on Pax Silica at the ASEAN Summit.
Trump will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China on Nov. 18 and 19.
